messages.subject: degrees of freedom (mediation model)
parts:
Hello! 

I don't quite understand why the degress of free is 0 based on the tutorial here. 

If we use the 3(3+1)/2 = 6 known parameters. 
3 beta coefficents to estimate and 2 residuals to estimate. 
Should that not be (6-5)=1 df left? 

I looked else where but the examples are quite difficult. A simpler model will be much easier to understand for me. 

Thank you!

set.seed(1234)
X <- rnorm(100)
M <- 0.5*X + rnorm(100)
Y <- 0.7*M + rnorm(100)
Data <- data.frame(X = X, Y = Y, M = M)
model <- ' # direct effect
             Y ~ c*X
           # mediator
             M ~ a*X
             Y ~ b*M
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)
         '
fit <- sem(model, data = Data)
summary(fit)

messages.subject: Re: degrees of freedom (mediation model)
parts: The other parameter is the (residual) variance of X. Every variable in the model gives rise to a free parameter for variance or residual variance, unless your model fixes that parameter. All estimated parameters count against degrees of freedom.
